<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:counterexample}
There exists a smooth quasi-projective toric Calabi--Yau threefold \(X\) with finite torus fixed locus such that the semigroup of compact effective curve classes is
\[
        \mathbb Z_{\geq0}[C_1]+\mathbb Z_{\geq0}[C_2],
\]
where \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are nonsingular compact torus-invariant curves that intersect transversely at a single torus fixed point \(v\).  Let
\[
        \beta=2[C_1]+[C_2],
        \qquad
        \gamma=[v]_T=i_{v*}(1).
\]
After restriction to the one-parameter subtorus whose tangent weights at \(v\) are \((1,2,-3)\), one has
\[
 [z^3]
 \left\langle\operatorname{ch}_z(\gamma)\right\rangle^{X,T,\mathrm{conn}}_{\beta}
 =
 \frac{18p^2}{(p-1)(p+1)^3}
 =
 \frac{9}{4}\frac{1}{p-1}+O(1)
\]
at \(p=1\).  Since \(\operatorname{div}(\beta)=1\), this pole is forbidden by Schimpf's connected pole restriction.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:geometry}
The variety \(X\) is a smooth quasi-projective toric Calabi--Yau threefold with finite torus fixed locus.  The semigroup of compact effective curve classes in \(H_2(X,\mathbb Z)/\mathrm{torsion}\) is
\[
      \operatorname{NE}(X)=\mathbb Z_{\geq0}[C_1]+\mathbb Z_{\geq0}[C_2],
\]
where \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are the two compact torus-invariant curves corresponding to the two interior edges of the triangulation.  The curves meet transversely at the torus fixed point \(v\) corresponding to the middle triangle.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The three triangles are unimodular, so the fan is smooth.  Since all primitive ray generators lie in the affine plane \(z=1\), the toric canonical class is trivial.  The torus fixed points correspond to the three maximal cones, hence \(X^T\) is finite.  Compact torus-invariant curves correspond to bounded edges of the triangulation, and the only bounded edges are the two displayed interior edges.  The toric Mori cone of this crepant \(A_2\)-chain resolution is generated by their classes.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:quotient}
The coefficients needed below are
\[
        C_{1,1}=F_{1,1}-Z_{1,0}F_{0,1}-Z_{0,1}F_{1,0}
\]
and
\begin{align}\label{eq:C21}
 C_{2,1}={}&F_{2,1}-Z_{0,1}F_{2,0}-Z_{1,0}F_{1,1}-Z_{2,0}F_{0,1}-Z_{1,1}F_{1,0} \notag\\
 &\quad +2Z_{1,0}Z_{0,1}F_{1,0}+Z_{1,0}^2F_{0,1}.
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Expand \(Z^{-1}=1-(Z-1)+(Z-1)^2-\cdots\) and extract \(Q_1Q_2\) and \(Q_1^2Q_2\).
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
We use Pandharipande--Thomas box configurations for the two-leg stable-pairs vertex \cite{PandharipandeThomasVertex}.  For fixed \((\lambda,\mu)\), the finite quotient monomials are described in Appendix~\ref{app:vertex}.  A stable-pairs configuration is an upward-closed finite subset of this finite-width partially ordered set.

For example, for \((2)|(1)\) there are two overlap monomials \(O_0,O_1\), with \(O_0\) forcing \(O_1\).  The possible overlap cases are
\[
        \varnothing,\qquad \{O_1\},\qquad \{O_0,O_1\}.
\]
The finite strings of quotient monomials in the negative \(C_1\)-direction have lengths \(a_0\leq a_1\), while the corresponding string in the negative \(C_2\)-direction has length \(b\).  Summing \((-p)^{\ell}\) over these cases gives the no-descendent two-leg vertex
\[
  1-\frac{p}{1+p}
  +\frac{p^2}{(1-p^2)(1+p)^2}
  =\frac{1+p-p^3}{1+2p-2p^3-p^4},
\]
which agrees with the entry \(P_{(2)|(1)}\) in Table~\ref{tab:nodesc-sums}.  For each finite configuration \(Q\), the finite character \(D_{\lambda|\mu,Q}\) is defined in Appendix~\ref{app:vertex}.  Taking the coefficient of \(z^3\) after this restriction gives a polynomial in the length parameters \(a_0,a_1,b\); summing the resulting geometric-power series gives the listed numerator.  The other seven pairs of relative partitions are computed by the same finite summation, with fewer overlap cases or fewer length parameters.

More explicitly, every entry is a finite \(\mathbb Q\)-linear combination of sums of the form
\[
   \sum_{a\geq0}a^r(-p)^a,\qquad
   \sum_{0\leq a\leq b}a^r b^s(-p)^{a+b},
\]
and products of these with the one-chain sums for the second leg.  These sums are evaluated by applying the operator \(r\frac{d}{dr}\) to \((1-r)^{-1}\) and to
\[
   \sum_{0\leq a\leq b}r^{a+b}
     =\frac{1}{(1-r)(1-r^2)}
\]
with \(r=-p\).  Thus the displayed rational functions are obtained by exact closed-form summation over all stable-pairs box configurations in the corresponding partially ordered sets.
The complete summation tables are given in Appendix~\ref{app:vertex}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:pole}
For the fixed-point descendent coefficient \([z^3]\operatorname{ch}_z([v]_T)\),
\[
       C_{1,1}=0,
       \qquad
       C_{2,1}=\frac{18p^2}{(p-1)(p+1)^3}
       =\frac{9}{4}\frac{1}{p-1}+O(1)
\]
at \(p=1\).
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
This is a direct substitution of Tables~\ref{tab:chain-weights} and~\ref{tab:desc-ratios} into \eqref{eq:C21}.  The bidegree aggregates are recorded in Appendix~\ref{app:laurent}.  They give
\[
       C_{1,1}=0,
       \qquad
       C_{2,1}=\frac{18p^2}{(p-1)(p+1)^3}.
\]
Thus all terms of order \((p-1)^{-3}\) and \((p-1)^{-2}\) cancel in the connected quotient, and the first nonzero Laurent term is
\[
       [ (p-1)^{-1}]\, C_{2,1}=\frac{9}{4}.
\]
The coefficient \(C_{1,1}\), corresponding to the class \([C_1]+[C_2]\), vanishes for this insertion.  Appendix~\ref{app:laurent} gives the term-by-term Laurent expansion.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:pole}, the connected single-insertion stable-pairs descendent coefficient in class
\[
        \beta=2[C_1]+[C_2]
\]
has a genuine pole at \(p=1\).  By \eqref{eq:div-one}, \(\operatorname{div}(\beta)=1\).  Therefore Schimpf's connected pole condition permits, away from \(p=0\), only the pole \(p=-1\).  Since \(p=1\) has \(-p=-1\), an order-two root of unity, it is forbidden for a class of divisibility one.  This is the claimed counterexample.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
